titleText.en: 'Hey Megan, it's your father. How do I print out a flowchart?'
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive title-text field is genuinely empty. The English text is the exact official xkcd image title attribute.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: dear (addressing a mixed or all-male plural group)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: At the start of a message, queridos warmly addresses the people named next. It is masculine plural because the addressed list is mixed or not limited to women.

example.en: Dear neighbors, thank you for coming.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: The masculine plural can mean grandfathers specifically or grandparents as a mixed group.

example.en: My grandparents live nearby.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: With de trabajo, compañeros means people who work with someone.

example.es: Mis compañeros de trabajo almuerzan aquí.
example.en: My coworkers have lunch here.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Here it describes plural feminine personas. Informático or informática can also name an IT professional.

example.es: Mis tías no son muy informáticas.
example.en: My aunts are not very computer-savvy.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: It describes an action as happening by magic or as if by magic.

example.es: La puerta no se abre mágicamente.
example.en: The door does not open magically.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ayudamos is the present form of ayudar used with nosotros or nosotras.

example.en: We help our neighbors.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: It describes what happens in the usual or expected way.

example.en: I usually arrive early.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Opción is a feminine noun, so it uses una or la.

example.en: We have another option.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: It can be a physical button or an on-screen control.

example.en: Press the green button.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: seems; looks (special form for a sought or unidentified thing)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Parezca is a form of parecer. It is used here because the speaker is looking for an option that has not yet been identified.

example.es: Busca un icono que parezca útil.
example.en: Look for an icon that seems useful.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Relacionado normally uses con before the other topic or thing.

example.es: El problema está relacionado con la red.
example.en: The problem is related to the network.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to; with (required after relacionado or relacionada)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish uses relacionado con where English usually says ‘related to.’

example.es: La noticia está relacionada con el clima.
example.en: The news is related to the climate.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: This is the present form of encontrar used with yo. It means locating something here, not considering it a certain way.

example.en: I cannot find my keys.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ninguno can stand alone for an understood masculine item. After a negative verb, English often uses ‘any.’

example.en: I cannot find any of them.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: This is the unchanged dictionary form ending in -ir.

example.en: You can choose an option.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: all of them (masculine or mixed plural)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Here todos stands alone for all the previously understood options.

example.en: I have tried all of them.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: press it; click it (informal singular command)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pulsa tells one familiar person to press or click. Lo means ‘it’ and attaches at the end; the written accent keeps the original stress.

example.en: If you see the button, press it.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Junto con introduces an additional person or thing included with the first one.

example.es: Escribe el nombre junto con la fecha.
example.en: Write the name together with the date.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Con remains unchanged in the expression junto con.

example.es: Envió la carta junto con una foto.
example.en: She sent the letter together with a photo.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: The -as ending matches a feminine plural noun such as palabras.

example.es: Son preguntas relacionadas con el trabajo.
example.en: They are questions related to work.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: people; one; you in general (impersonal marker)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Before a third-person singular verb, se can leave the people doing the action unspecified.

example.en: People work a lot here.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: one wants; people want (after impersonal se)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Quiere is third-person singular because impersonal se leaves the person unspecified.

example.es: Cuando se quiere aprender, hay que practicar.
example.en: When one wants to learn, one has to practice.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: This feminine plural noun refers to steps that tell someone what to do.

example.es: Sigue las instrucciones de la pantalla.
example.en: Follow the instructions on the screen.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: you have spent; you have been at (for a duration)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With a span of time, llevas says how long one familiar person has already spent on something.

example.es: Llevas una hora con ese informe.
example.en: You have been working on that report for an hour.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Media agrees with the feminine noun hora. Medio is used before a masculine noun.

example.en: I waited half an hour.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Funcionado is the completed-action form of funcionar and follows a form of haber.

example.en: The plan has worked.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Rendir becomes rendirse in this meaning. The short marker se attaches to the dictionary form.

example.en: He does not want to give up.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Standing alone, ¡hecho! announces that a task is complete. This differs from hecho after haber in he hecho, ‘I have done.’

example.en: Done! You can rest now.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: print (positive command to several people, mainly in Spain)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Replace imprimir's final -r with -d to make the vosotros command.

example.en: Print the form.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: stick it; attach it (command to several people, mainly in Spain)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pegad is the vosotros command of pegar. Lo means ‘it’ and attaches to the end.

example.en: Stick it on the wall.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Cerca normally uses de before the nearby person, place, or thing.

example.es: La estación está cerca de casa.
example.en: The station is near home.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Monitor is masculine: el monitor.

example.en: The monitor is on.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Use ¡felicidades! to congratulate someone on good news or an achievement.

example.en: Congratulations on the prize!

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Here informático describes an expert's technical field. As a noun, informático can also mean a male IT professional.

example.en: We need IT support.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you refer to a coworker or colleague?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Say compañero de trabajo for a man and compañera de trabajo for a woman; use the plural compañeros or compañeras de trabajo.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The person word changes for gender and number. De trabajo stays unchanged and identifies the shared workplace relationship.

example.es: Una compañera de trabajo me ayudó.
example.en: A coworker helped me.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that one topic or thing is related to another?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use relacionado, relacionada, relacionados, or relacionadas to match the first thing, then con before the related topic.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Only relacionado changes for gender and number. Con stays unchanged; English commonly uses ‘related to’ rather than ‘related with.’

example.es: La pregunta está relacionada con el examen.
example.en: The question is related to the exam.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone or something is included together with another item?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use junto con, followed by the additional person or thing.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Junto con stays together as a connector. It can often be translated as ‘together with’ or simply ‘along with.’

example.es: Mandó el informe junto con las fotos.
example.en: She sent the report along with the photos.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: se + verbo en tercera persona singular (persona no especificada)
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can Spanish describe what people in general, an unspecified person, or ‘you’ generally do?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Put se before a third-person singular verb and leave the person unspecified.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: This impersonal pattern focuses on the action rather than naming who performs it: aquí se trabaja means ‘people work here.’ It is distinct from the reflexive use in which someone acts on themself.

example.es: En esta biblioteca se estudia en silencio.
example.en: People study quietly in this library.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say how long someone has already spent working on or dealing with something?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of llevar, state the duration, then use con before the activity or thing occupying that time.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Llevar changes for the person: llevo, llevas, lleva, and so on. The duration states the elapsed time, while con introduces what has occupied it.

example.es: Llevamos dos horas con esta tarea.
example.en: We have been working on this task for two hours.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone asks another person for help?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use pedir ayuda, then a before the person being asked.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pedir changes for the person and time. Ayuda stays singular in this expression, and a introduces the person asked for help.

example.es: Voy a pedir ayuda a mi vecina.
example.en: I am going to ask my neighbor for help.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: cerca de + persona, lugar o cosa
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone or something is near a person, place, or thing?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use cerca de, followed by the nearby person, place, or thing.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Cerca is followed by de in this pattern. When el follows, de + el contracts to del: cerca del parque.

example.en: We live near the station.

Imprimid replaces imprimir's final -r with -d to address several people informally.
The -d ending marks a positive command addressed to vosotros or vosotras, mainly in Spain.
Diagrama is the main noun, de links it to its type, and flujo identifies the process-flow kind of diagram.
Pegad is the positive command for several informal listeners, and lo attaches to identify what they should stick up.
The -d command ending addresses several people informally in the form used mainly in Spain.
Cerca de introduces the nearby reference point, and vuestro monitor supplies that complete place or thing.
Vuestro addresses several people informally and matches the one masculine singular monitor possessed.
Sois is the present form of ser for several people addressed informally, mainly in Spain.
Informático and local both follow the noun experto and describe its field and scope.
Informático is masculine singular to match experto, while local has one gender form and remains singular.
